The main takeaway from our work is that
the CGM of massive galaxies at high redshift is a reservoir of heavy elements that is enriched by a combination of early outflows, late superwinds, and infalling satellite galaxies.

the enrichment of the CGM of massive galaxies at high redshifts is dominated by the metals shed by their progenitors, which can be dwarf galaxies or even smaller systems, and not by the outflows generated by their recent star formation.

the metal content of massive galaxies is determined by their assembly history, with the bulk of metals being ejected at high redshifts, and that their circumgalactic medium is enriched not only by their own outflows, but also by those of nearby dwarfs.
